title: Embedding a system of abelian sheaves on an inverse system of sites into a system of injectives
statement: In the situation of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites] (a cofiltered category $\mathcal I$, sites $\mathcal C_i$ whose coverings have finite index sets, morphisms of sites $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ for $a:j\to i$ given by continuous functors $u_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ with $u_b\circ u_a=u_{a\circ b}$, the colimit site $\mathcal C=\varinjlim\mathcal C_i$ with the canonical functors $u_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C$, $u_j\circ u_a=u_i$, and the morphisms of sites $f_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_i$ they define [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]), let $\mathcal F_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C_i$ for every $i$ and $\varphi_a:f_a^{-1}\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_j$ ($a:j\to i$) maps of abelian sheaves with $\varphi_{a\circ b}=\varphi_b\circ f_b^{-1}\varphi_a$. Then there are abelian sheaves $\mathcal G_i$ on $\mathcal C_i$, maps $\psi_a:f_a^{-1}\mathcal G_i\to\mathcal G_j$ with $\psi_{a\circ b}=\psi_b\circ f_b^{-1}\psi_a$, and injective maps of abelian sheaves $\gamma_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal G_i$ forming a map of systems ($\psi_a\circ f_a^{-1}\gamma_i=\gamma_j\circ\varphi_a$ for all $a:j\to i$), such that every $\mathcal G_i$ is an injective object of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C_i)$. (Stacks' construction: $\mathcal G_i=\prod_{b:k\to i}f_{b*}\mathcal A_k$ for chosen injective embeddings $\mathcal F_k\to\mathcal A_k$; $f_{b*}$ preserves injectives because $f_b^{-1}$ is exact, and products of injectives are injective.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EXZ (lemma-colim-sites-injective) and its proof (Lemma Tag 0730 lemma-pushforward-injective-flat, Homology Lemma Tag 0137 lemma-product-injectives, Homology Lemma Tag 015Z lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives)

proof.text: For each index $i$, the enough-injectives hypothesis on $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C_i)$ supplies an injective embedding $\gamma_i^0:\mathcal F_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal A_i$. For every arrow $b:k\to i$, compose the transition map $\varphi_b:f_b^{-1}\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_k$ with $\gamma_k^0$ and take its adjoint under $f_b^{-1}\dashv f_{b*}$; this gives a map $\mathcal F_i\to f_{b*}\mathcal A_k$. The family of these maps defines $\gamma_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal G_i$, where $\mathcal G_i:=\prod_{b:k\to i}f_{b*}\mathcal A_k$.

Each $f_{b*}\mathcal A_k$ is injective: $f_b^{-1}$ is exact by the definition of a morphism of sites, and the right-adjoint criterion for exact functors applies to $f_b^{-1}\dashv f_{b*}$. Hence $\mathcal G_i$, a set-indexed product of injectives, is injective by the product-of-injectives lemma.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EXZ proof, final sentence; Homology Tags 0137 and 015Z

proof.text: For an arrow $a:j\to i$, define $\psi_a:f_a^{-1}\mathcal G_i\to\mathcal G_j$ componentwise: the component indexed by $b:k\to j$ is the canonical map from $f_a^{-1}f_{a\circ b,*}\mathcal A_k$ to $f_{b,*}\mathcal A_k$, obtained from the composition identity for the inverse-image functors and the adjunctions. Reindexing by composition shows $\psi_{a\circ b}=\psi_b\circ f_b^{-1}\psi_a$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EXZ proof, displayed definition of psi_a

proof.text: The maps $\gamma_i$ form a map of systems by adjunction naturality and the cocycle identity $\varphi_{a\circ b}=\varphi_b\circ f_b^{-1}\varphi_a$. The component indexed by $\operatorname{id}_i:i\to i$ is the chosen monomorphism $\gamma_i^0$, so each $\gamma_i$ is a monomorphism. Thus $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_a)$ embeds into the system $(\mathcal G_i,\psi_a)$ of injective sheaves.
